newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QNI sees subdued nickel price.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QNI sees subdued nickel price.

text.p: The chairman of Australian nickel and cobalt producer QNI Ltd, Max Roberts, said on Tuesday he did not agree with market analysts' expectations of an improvement in nickel prices by the end of next year.
"The forecast is for improving (nickel) prices. I frankly don't believe it," he told the group's annual meeting.
Roberts said after the meeting that QNI was in for a tough year but would record a profit for the 12 months ended June 30.
"Yes, we will be in profit," Roberts told reporters.

"If you come up with a good exchange rate, then we're smelling of roses," Roberts said. Shareholders were told earlier that QNI was not expecting profit for the current year to match the group's 1995/96 performance.
Managing director Wyn Davies said the group was also looking at doing some processing at its ore sites in New Caledonia in addition to shipping ore to its Yabalu refinery in Queensland.
Roberts earlier estimated there could be cost savings of up to 60 percent if ore could be partially treated at the source.
QNI had looked at setting up its own mine and production facilities in New Caledonia but was facing capital costs of up to A$1 billion, Roberts said.
"Partial treatment is the answer," he said.

Davies said the recently-announced joint study on potential developments in Indonesia with Indonesian state-owned mining group Aneka Tambang and Gencor Ltd of South Africa looked like developing into a firm project. "Nothing we've seen has deterred our enthusiasm," Davies said. The scoping study was progressing well and was expected to be completed by March next year, he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
